# Keisha Lance Bottoms Watchdog File

Subject: Keisha Lance Bottoms, Democratic nominee for Governor of Georgia, 2026
Compiled: October 23, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us
Data cutoff: October 22, 2026. The latest filed Georgia figures run through July 31, 2026. Later figures are campaign announcements.
Next scheduled data drop: the Georgia report covering activity through October 20, 2026, due the week of October 26 according to the AJC. The exact due date was not verified.

## Bottom line up front

1. The Democratic Governors Association is her financial base. It gave more than $1.6 million to her leadership committee in June and July, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/). Her campaign then said the DGA gave $11.5 million of the $23.2 million she raised from August 1 to October 20, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-fundraising/). The October figures are provisional until the filing lands.
2. Billionaire Democrats arrived late. JB Pritzker gave $1 million to her leadership fund after the October 20 cutoff, and Michael Bloomberg gave at least $1 million, per the [AJC on October 21](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/).
3. Her signature policy fights put her against large industries: a statewide pause on new data center construction, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/10/poll-georgians-government-regulation-of-ai/); Medicaid expansion, per her [AJC column](https://www.ajc.com/opinion/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-affordability-georgia/); and ending the 2.25 percent auto insurance premium tax, per [FOX 5](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor-candidate-profile). No donors from those industries were documented on either side.
4. Real estate is a small but traceable bloc, at least $30,000 from commercial real estate figures through July, per [Bisnow](https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/economic-development/jackson-far-outraising-bottoms-georgia-governor-race-cre-execs-donations-campaign-finance). Her record as mayor includes a long term downtown redevelopment deal.
5. Disclosure history is the opening for critics: a $37,000 state ethics fine in 2021 for her 2017 race, a $125 late filing fine in 2026, and paid property tax liens reported by the AJC in October.

## Committee structure and treasurer

Bottoms runs a capped Georgia candidate committee, opened in spring 2025, and Project Battleground Georgia, a leadership committee she created after winning the May 19, 2026 primary outright, per the [Georgia Recorder](https://cobbcountycourier.com/2026/08/gop-candidates-outraise-democrats-so-far-in-most-but-not-all-of-georgias-statewide-contests/). Georgia's 2021 law lets the two parties' nominees for governor run leadership committees that take unlimited gifts. Project Battleground Georgia had raised more than $3 million by July 31 and at least $3.4 million by mid September, per the AJC. Her campaign committee raised $5.7 million from May 6, 2025 through July 31, 2026 and held just over $770,000 at the end of July, per [Capitol Beat](https://roughdraftatlanta.com/2026/08/11/rick-jackson-outpaces-bottoms-fundraising/). The AJC put cash on hand at about $1.3 million for the same date, a difference likely explained by counting both accounts.

The treasurer, the state filer IDs and any compliance firm were not found because the state commission site refused automated access. Communications director TaNisha Cameron speaks for the campaign. Bottoms lent her campaign $200,000 in its first half year, per [FOX 5](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-jason-esteves-fundraising-georgia-governor-race), a campaign announcement made before the filing.

## Party and leadership: the DGA

Documented. DGA money reached Project Battleground Georgia in the June 11 to July 31 period. The AJC reported more than $1.6 million and the Georgia Recorder about $1.8 million; the outlets differ. For August 1 to October 20 her campaign reported $11.5 million from the DGA, the largest single source, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-fundraising/). The DGA also pledged to spend at least $10 million for her and said "Republicans are drastically outspending us." Sen. Jon Ossoff said he moved more than $3.6 million over two years to the Democratic Party of Georgia's coordinated campaign, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/09/can-keisha-lance-bottoms-withstand-rick-jacksons-spending-blitz-in-georgia/). That money supports the ticket and is not stored as a gift to Bottoms.

What they want and the lever. The party's ask is the seat itself: the first Democratic governor since Roy Barnes, per the AJC. The governor's veto, budget and appointments are the lever.

Inference: by her own numbers the DGA supplied about half of her late money, so the national party has more invested in her than any Georgia donor documented here.

## Billionaire megadonors

Documented. Pritzker gave $1 million to the leadership fund, and Bloomberg gave at least $1 million, which her campaign confirmed; the AJC cited Politico and the New York Times, which were not read. Pritzker also gave $100,000 to Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek this month, per a [Willamette Week](https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-gives-100k-to-kotek/) headline only.

The lever. Neither donor has a documented Georgia business ask in the sources read. Bloomberg's known causes and Pritzker's are not stored here without a source.

Inference: these look like party building gifts to a toss up race, not bloc purchases. They should be watched on the filing for the account and date.

## Real estate and development

Documented. Through July, commercial real estate donors gave Bottoms at least $30,000, per [Bisnow](https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/economic-development/jackson-far-outraising-bottoms-georgia-governor-race-cre-execs-donations-campaign-finance): Ronald Abramson of Buchanan $31,400, Gerald Alley of Con-Real $8,400 in June, Rod Mullice of Windsor Stevens Holdings more than $5,000, and Egbert Perry of Integral Group $2,500. Perry also gave Jackson $2,000. Avison Young's Kirk Rich hosted a fundraiser. Six figure checks to her leadership committee came from Sycamore Management at $100,000 and Matthew Bernstein at $50,000, per the AJC; their businesses were not resolved. Education Reform Now PAC and EMILY's List gave $25,000 each.

The lever. She proposes a statewide affordable housing trust fund and a higher homestead exemption. As Recreation Authority director she helped broker the Turner Field sale, and as mayor she helped negotiate a long term downtown redevelopment, per [FOX 5](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor-candidate-profile) and the [AP](https://newspressnow.com/?p=57692).

Inference: the dollar amounts are small. The bloc matters more as a relationship network from her Atlanta years than as a funding source.

## Own finances and disclosure history

No net worth estimate or state financial disclosure was found. Details about a family member who is not a political actor are left out. The AJC reported in October 2026 that more than a dozen property tax and HOA liens totaling over $47,000 since 2010 were recorded on household properties and that all were paid, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-and-her-husband-have-a-history-of-late-tax-payments/). Her campaign said she paid her taxes and pointed to Jackson's IRS dispute.

## Enforcement and controversies

2017 mayoral campaign. In 2021 her campaign agreed to a $37,000 state ethics fine. The commission's director called some of the violations procedural. No direct response from Bottoms was found.

2026 late filing. Her July 31 report came in a day after the grace period and carries a $125 fine. The campaign blamed a technical error, per the Georgia Recorder.

2021 refunds. Her mayoral account reported more than $413,000 in spending including refunds of 238 donations after she declined to run again, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/news/atlanta-news/atlanta-mayor-returns-413000-in-campaign-refunds/WAHEOKFRLRAT5J4SWYGWTLVJEM/). No finding of wrongdoing was reported.

Record as mayor. Jackson's ads attack her public safety record. An AJC analysis found Atlanta homicides rose 59 percent from 2019 to 2020. Bottoms cites the pandemic and points to police raises and the training center. A federal corruption probe of her predecessor's administration overshadowed her first term, per the AP. She is not reported as a target.

National Guard. She said Jackson promised to send the Guard during the election. Jackson called it "a complete falsehood." The claim is stored as contested.

## Deal table

| Interest | Money in | Ask | Lever | Stake | Decision date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Democratic Governors Association | $1.6M to $1.8M June to July; $11.5M Aug to Oct 20, provisional | Win the seat | Veto, budget, appointments | Party control of Georgia executive | November 3, 2026 |
| Billionaire Democrats | Pritzker $1M; Bloomberg at least $1M | Not stated | Not documented | Not quantified | November 3, 2026 |
| Real estate and developers | At least $30K through July | Housing and redevelopment policy | Housing trust fund, homestead exemption | Not quantified | 2027 session |
| Education Reform Now PAC | $25K | Education policy | School funding formula | Not quantified | 2027 session |
| Unresolved six figure donors | Sycamore Management $100K, Matthew Bernstein $50K | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Levers and calendar

| Decision | Who holds it now | When | Donors who care |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid expansion | Governor, DCH, legislature | 2027 session | None documented |
| Data center construction pause | PSC, legislature, local governments | 2027 session | None documented |
| Auto insurance premium tax and gas tax | Legislature | 2027 session | None documented |
| Casino referendum with pre-K revenue | Legislature must refer | 2027 or 2028 session | None documented |
| Housing trust fund and homestead exemption | Legislature | 2027 session | Real estate donors |
| School funding formula | Governor, legislature | 2027 session | Education Reform Now PAC |
| State Election Board abolition | Legislature | 2027 session | Ideological groups |

Calendar: November 3, 2026 general election, with a runoff possible if no one tops 50 percent; the runoff date was not verified. The pre-general report lands the week of October 26 and should confirm the DGA, Bloomberg and $23.2 million figures. Pritzker's gift lands on a later report. The governor takes office in January 2027 and the 2027 session follows. A casino amendment would need legislative referral in 2027 or 2028.

## What we could not verify

The Georgia Ethics Commission site refused automated fetches, so no filing was read. Missing: committee IDs, treasurer, the October report and any financial disclosure. Not read: Politico on Pritzker and the New York Times on Bloomberg, cited by the AJC with no link seen; [Willamette Week](https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-gives-100k-to-kotek/), which failed to load; the factually.co fact check; wikipedia.org, blocked; WRDW and Atlanta News First 2025 launch coverage. DGA funders, the businesses of Sycamore Management and Matthew Bernstein, her vendors, consultants and pollsters, and any net worth figure were not found in this pass.

# Keisha Lance Bottoms research notes

Compiled October 23, 2026. Shared tool budget with the Jackson file. The web search budget ran out early, so the work relied on WebFetch of surfaced and AJC linked pages. No Georgia filing was read because ethics.ga.gov refused fetches.

## Thread 1: Committees and IDs

### Takeaway
Candidate committee opened in spring 2025 and Project Battleground Georgia, a leadership committee formed after the May 19 2026 primary win.

### Cited findings
- Project Battleground Georgia created after she became nominee; about $1.8M from DGA; late filing and $125 fine; campaign blamed technical error. Georgia Recorder via Cobb Courier Aug 12 2026: https://cobbcountycourier.com/2026/08/gop-candidates-outraise-democrats-so-far-in-most-but-not-all-of-georgias-statewide-contests/
- Leadership committee more than $3M since June; $5.6M raised in period; cash about $1.3M. AJC Aug 8 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/
- At least $3.4M through the leadership committee by mid September. AJC Sept 17 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/09/can-keisha-lance-bottoms-withstand-rick-jacksons-spending-blitz-in-georgia/
- $3.1M May to July; $5.7M since May 6 2025; cash just over $770,000; corporate a little over $360,000; about $2.3M out of state. Capitol Beat Aug 11 2026: https://roughdraftatlanta.com/2026/08/11/rick-jackson-outpaces-bottoms-fundraising/ ; FOX 5 Aug 12 2026: https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/rick-jackson-outraises-bottoms-georgia-governor-race
- Filed papers in 2025. AP via News-Press Now: https://newspressnow.com/?p=57692

### Inferences
Inference: the AJC and Capitol Beat cash figures differ because one counts both accounts.

### Gaps
Treasurer; filer IDs; compliance firm.

## Thread 2: Money in

### Takeaway
DGA first, billionaires late, small six figure checks otherwise.

### Cited findings
- DGA more than $1.6M; Sycamore Management $100,000; Matthew Bernstein $50,000; Education Reform Now PAC and EMILY's List $25,000 each. AJC Aug 8 2026, link above.
- $23.2M Aug 1 to Oct 20 per campaign, DGA $11.5M, Bloomberg at least $1M, Pritzker $1M after the Oct 20 deadline, filing due next week. AJC, announced Thursday Oct 22 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-fundraising/
- Pritzker $1M to leadership fund; Bloomberg at least $1M; DGA pledged at least $10M; about $10M raised through campaign accounts. AJC Oct 21 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/
- $1.1M Feb to Jun 2025 including a $200,000 loan; nearly 7,100 donors; campaign announcement. FOX 5 Jul 4 2025: https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-jason-esteves-fundraising-georgia-governor-race
- $1.1M July 2025 to Jan 31 2026; about $810,000 cash. AJC Feb 2026: https://feeds.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/republicans-report-more-cash-than-democrats-in-races-for-two-top-georgia-offices
- CRE donors: Abramson $31,400; Mullice more than $5,000; Alley $8,400 June; Zoukis $1,000 July; Effron $1,000 July; Perry $2,500; Kirk Rich hosted; at least $30K total. Bisnow Aug 16 2026: https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/economic-development/jackson-far-outraising-bottoms-georgia-governor-race-cre-execs-donations-campaign-finance
- Nearly $6M raised per disclosures as of Sept 7 2026. Atlanta News First: https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/09/07/negative-blitzes-foster-youth-testimonials-georgia-voters-flooded-by-record-breaking-ad-war/

### Inferences
Inference: the AJC Oct 21 figure of about $10M through campaign accounts and the Oct 22 figure of $23.2M since August cannot both describe the same period; the Oct 21 figure likely predates the campaign announcement. Use the filing to settle it.

### Gaps
Who Sycamore Management and Matthew Bernstein are; DGA's own funders; Bloomberg's receiving account and date.

## Thread 3: Money out

### Takeaway
Thin. She spent about $2.6M to win the nomination and had $42,000 in TV reserved as of mid September.

### Cited findings
About $2.6M primary spending, AJC Jul 2 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/ . $42,000 reserved, Bottoms and allies about $8M versus nearly $76M pro-Jackson, AJC Sept 17 2026 link above. 2021 mayoral account: more than $413,000 spending including 238 refunds; nearly $74,000 financing and consulting; nearly $17,000 legal; nearly $20,000 ActBlue fees. AJC Jul 13 2021: https://www.ajc.com/news/atlanta-news/atlanta-mayor-returns-413000-in-campaign-refunds/WAHEOKFRLRAT5J4SWYGWTLVJEM/

### Inferences
Inference: her late money will mostly show up as late TV buys on the October report.

### Gaps
Vendors, media buyer, pollster names. Strategists named in AJC Sept 17, Tharon Johnson, Scott Paradise and Falak Sabbak, were not confirmed as paid Bottoms consultants, so no edge was stored.

## Thread 4: Own finances

### Takeaway
No disclosure or net worth found. AJC documented paid liens.

### Cited findings
More than a dozen liens since 2010 totaling over $47,000, all paid; HOA lien Sept 2025 paid in two weeks; 2017 water bill dispute. AJC Oct 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-and-her-husband-have-a-history-of-late-tax-payments/ . Details about a non political family member and a health related explanation in that article are deliberately not stored.

### Inferences
None.

### Gaps
State financial disclosure; income from CNN and White House roles.

## Thread 5: Enforcement and controversies

### Takeaway
Small dollar disclosure problems, repeated.

### Cited findings
$37,000 ethics fine agreed 2021 for 2017 race, director called some violations procedural; homicide rise 59 percent 2019 to 2020 and her response. FOX 5 profile: https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor-candidate-profile . $125 late fine, Georgia Recorder link above. Federal corruption probe under Kasim Reed overshadowed start of her term, AP link above. National Guard claim and Jackson denial, Atlanta News First Oct 6 2026: https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/video/2026/10/07/bottoms-says-jackson-promises-send-national-guard-during-election/

### Inferences
Inference: Jackson's campaign is already using the $37,000 fine, per spokesman Garrison Douglas in the Georgia Recorder.

### Gaps
Commission case number for the 2017 matter; any 2026 complaints.

## Thread 6: Hop two

### Takeaway
Little hop two is traceable without search.

### Cited findings
Ossoff more than $3.6M to the Democratic Party of Georgia coordinated campaign, AJC Sept 17 2026 link above. Pritzker $100,000 to Kotek, headline only: https://www.wweek.com/news/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-gives-100k-to-kotek/ , fetch failed. Perry gave to both nominees, Bisnow link above.

### Inferences
None.

### Gaps
DGA donors; Bloomberg's other 2026 state gifts; Education Reform Now PAC funders.

## Thread 7: Levers

### Takeaway
Medicaid expansion, data center pause, insurance and gas tax cuts, casino referendum, housing trust fund.

### Cited findings
Pause on data centers. AJC Oct 22 2026: https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/10/poll-georgians-government-regulation-of-ai/ . Medicaid, grocery tax, auto and homeowner insurance tax, gas tax, housing trust fund, homestead exemption, pre-K. AJC column Oct 2026: https://www.ajc.com/opinion/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-affordability-georgia/ . Casino vote with pre-K revenue, State Election Board abolition, $15 minimum wage, ICE and Atlanta jail. FOX 5 profile link above. Medicaid and Ossoff ticket. AJC Jun 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/06/keisha-lance-bottoms-is-in-for-a-very-different-race-against-rick-jackson/

### Inferences
Inference: none of her biggest documented donors has a stated stake in these levers; the data center and insurance positions run against industries that have not shown up in her receipts.

### Gaps
Positions on PSC appointments, film tax credit, Georgia Power.

## Thread 8: Votes and record

### Takeaway
Record is executive: Atlanta mayor 2018 to 2022, city council 2009 onward, White House Office of Public Engagement director.

### Cited findings
FOX 5 profile and AP links above. Ended cash bail and the city jail's relationship with federal immigration agencies; negotiated a downtown redevelopment; Amazon HQ2 went elsewhere. AP link above. DNC vice chair nomination, Atlanta Black Star, undated: https://atlantablackstar.com/?p=562700

### Inferences
None.

### Gaps
Specific redevelopment deal terms and the developers who benefited; council votes.
